newsitem.title: USA: FAA approves Newark, N.J., airport rail link.
newsitem.headline: FAA approves Newark, N.J., airport rail link.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration Thursday approved a $250 million rail link to New Jersey's Newark Airport, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said.
The project, which is being funded through $3 federal surcharges on passenger tickets, will now begin with site preparation and contruction. The project is set to go into service in mid-2000.
"What we are doing in Newark mirrors access improvement under way for the New York airports," said Port Authority Chairman Lewis Eisenberg.

"The agency is moving aggressively to build a light rail system that will link JFK (International Airport) to a nearby rail and subway hub, and to provide high-speed ferry service from points in Manhattan to LaGuardia Airport," Eisenberg said.
